identity: A Palestinian primary-school worksheet / exam page on plants and agriculture (heritage + basic botany). Not prose: it is 16 true-false items, each 'statement + صح + خطأ' answer boxes, plus 4 multiple-choice items, each 'stem + three options'. One item per line, so every <NL> closes one item. This is doctrine section J territory: layout IS content, the page furniture IS the sentence. LAW 6 register target is the shortest band in the corpus (3-10 tokens), and here most units are one-word answer labels, so mean segment length lands near 2 real tokens.
law: Reconstruct the ink of a worksheet page, not the meaning of a paragraph. Three unit types: (1) the STATEMENT or STEM is one segment, terminated by the source period or by the colon/blank that hands off to the options; (2) each ANSWER OPTION is its own segment, because on the page each sits in its own box or cell (صح ( ) خطأ ( ), or option - option - option) and doctrine J2 cut every cell of a two-cell row in doc_70d28c9dfebb; (3) the token before each <NL> and the final token are free boundaries. Asyndetic parallel option lists cut under LAW 3. Phrase-level و joining two nouns or two adjectives never cuts (والفراولة, وأوراق, ومفيدة). A trailing purpose or adjunct clause stays with its main clause under LAW 4 (لينمو).
reasoning: SITE 1, the ruling that decides this document: do صح and خطأ split from each other and from the statement? Splitting from the statement is forced twice over -- the statement is a complete nominal or verbal sentence that cannot be grammatically continued into صح, and the source printed a period or a column break there. Splitting صح from خطأ is the real question, and it recurs 16 times, so it dominates F1. I split, on three grounds. (a) Direct precedent: doctrine J2, doc_70d28c9dfebb @102/@104, where a two-cell row went to gold as المفردة | تفسيرها | وفى | عهده -- every cell its own segment. صح ( ) خطأ ( ) is the same object: two boxed alternatives with ink (parentheses, cell border, wide gap) between them. (b) LAW 0 corollary lists a table break as one of the marks that became a boundary. (c) LAW 3: two adjacent items, no connective, identical parallel frame, mutually exclusive -- that is rhetorical listing, and gold cuts listing. I considered the counter-precedent J6, where a slogan strip stayed whole, and rejected it: a slogan is a continuous banner phrase read left to right, whereas صح/خطأ are two discrete checkbox labels. Consistency then forces the same treatment on the MC option triples -- if صح | خطأ splits, then الذرة | الفجل | الجزر splits. || SITE 2, index 10, the only genuinely uncertain site in 152 tokens: القمباز من التراث وترتديه النساء. This is the sole place in the whole document where LAW 1 can fire -- وترتديه carries a fresh finite verb AND a new subject النساء, which is exactly LAW 1's new-argument test. Every other و here is phrase-level and exempt: والفراولة (noun+noun), وأوراق (noun+noun), ومفيدة (adj+adj). Against cutting: this is a single T/F item that the student must judge as one compound claim, and a five-word worksheet item carries exactly one period, at its end -- no Arabic worksheet author commas before وترتديه, so on a pure ink reading there is nothing there. For cutting: LAW 1 is my highest-yield law by a wide margin (about 120 of my 231 batch-1 misses), J7 explicitly confirms LAW 1 survives in textbook material over six instances, and LAW 0 says my base rate is 5-to-1 under-cutting so a formally-firing LAW 1 site should default to CUT. I cut, at lo confidence, and flag it as the single site in this document I most want graded against me. Note that its isolation is itself evidence about the page: this worksheet is written in one-clause items, and item 2 is the author's one lapse into a two-predicate item. || SITE 3, the MC stems. Item 7 (نباتات لا تؤكل جذورها) ends in a clean colon after a complete NP description -- hi. Items 9 and 10 end mid-construction: تبدأ حياة النبتة من ends on the preposition من, and نضع النبات في مكان ends on the head noun مكان whose three options are adjectives modifying it. Both are fill-in-the-blank shapes, and J4 (doc_32908af53b40 @534) rules that the blank itself is the boundary: gold cut تقع دولة الإمارات ... إلى جهة | من شبه الجزيرة العربية mid-construction exactly this way. So I cut at من (66) and at مكان (74), med confidence, because the noun-adjective reading مكان مشمس is a live alternative parse. || SITE 4, LAW 4 checks. Item 4, يحتاج النبات إلى هواء لينمو: لينمو is a trailing purpose clause, so no cut before it, the cut goes after it at 28. Item 17, جذور النباتات متنوعة ومفيدة: ومفيدة is a bare coordinate adjective sharing the subject, LAW 1's exception, so no cut, boundary at 128. Item 11, نأكل ساق وأوراق ثمرة الكوسا: وأوراق coordinates two nouns inside one object NP, no cut, boundary at 83. || SITE 5, index 103-107, بعد الزيتون من النباتات الموسم, is garbled OCR of يعد الزيتون من النباتات الموسمية. I segment the surface form as written -- one statement, boundary at 107 (الموسم) -- and do not repair it, since the annotation tracks the ink on the page. || Density check: 65 boundaries over 133 non-<NL> tokens, mean 2.05 real tokens per segment. That looks extreme until you note that 44 of the 65 segments are single-word answer options, while the 20 statement/stem segments run 4-5 tokens each, sitting squarely in the J band of 3-10.
